reputation.millenaire.norman.friend_of_v: We are not known for trusting people easily, but my good friend $name, you have really shown we can trust you!
reputation.millenaire.norman.ally.descri: In this strange world, everyone needs allies. Consider us one, for all of the help you have given us.
reputation.millenaire.norman.one_of_us.d: It's always a pleasure to see you $name. You may come from distant lands, but you are really one of us now.
reputation.millenaire.norman.natural_lea: $name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Normans. They will follow you anywhere.
reputation.millenaire.indian.public_enem: Every morning I pray the Goddess I will never see your face again.
reputation.millenaire.indian.unpleasant_: Whoever raised you did a very poor job. We hope you will be gone soon.
reputation.millenaire.indian.nuisance.de: We do not like foreigners here, especially of your kind.
reputation.millenaire.indian.stranger.de: We are not used to foreigners in our remote village.
reputation.millenaire.indian.familiarity: So far, you have not committed any major breach of custom.

reputation.millenaire.indian.favourite_t: Welcome back, $name. What have you brought to trade with us?
reputation.millenaire.indian.friend_of_v: $name-ji, we all consider you a true friend here.
reputation.millenaire.indian.ally.descri: You are a true ally of this village $name-ji! If you ever need refuge, you can stay in our village.
reputation.millenaire.indian.one_of_us.d: I would not thought I would live to see a foreign accepted in the village, but $name-ji, you are one of us now!
reputation.millenaire.indian.natural_lea: $name-ji, you have gained the trust and respect of my people. They will follow you anywhere.

reputation.millenaire.byzantines.public_: It was embarrassing of the whole Roman empire to let you alive. While you continue to enjoy to live, leave the Roman lands and never return.

reputation.millenaire.byzantines.known_f: Other Romans seem to have noticed you and they speak well of you! You don't seem to be a barbarian after all.
reputation.millenaire.byzantines.regular: Xaire, $name! Nice to see you. How are things?
reputation.millenaire.byzantines.fellow_: Ah, it's good to see that others outside of the Roman Empire can be civilized like us once in a while.

reputation.millenaire.byzantines.friend_: You are part of our village $name, we trust you now!

reputation.millenaire.byzantines.natural: $name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Byzantines. They will follow you anywhere.

reputation.millenaire.seljuk.nuisance.de: We don't want any trouble here.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.stranger.de: God bless you, stranger! Be on your best behavior and we'll stay on friendly terms.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.familiarity: Welcome! Feel free to stay here to get out from under the hot sun, traveller.
Ah, $name, it is good to see you again. Any interesting stories to tell?
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.regular_vis: The people of the village seem to be warming up to you. Keep it up and you'll have friends for life.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.fellow_wand: Everyone is on their own journey through life, and we're glad to know that you've been willing to join us on ours.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.favourite_t: We look forward to seeing what you've brought with you today! Anything new?
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.friend_of_v: God brought you to us, and we're very glad that He did, friend.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.respectable: We Turks are not known for being the most trusting of outsiders, but we're more than happy to know that we can call you one of our closest allies.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.one_of_us.d: You might not have been born a Turk, $name, but as far as I can tell, you're just as Seljuk as anyone else here.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.natural_lea: $name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Seljuks. They will follow you anywhere.
reputation.millenaire.seljuk.next_great_: While some may object, we all know that there's no one better than you to carry out the will of God and of the Turkish people.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.public_enem: We've given you plenty of chances to commune with us, but you've shunned our efforts. Leave us be and hope the spirits don't take you as you wander the frozen wastes.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.unpleasant_: We're wary of people like you. Just go away and leave us in peace.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.nuisance.de: Please, we have no time for people like you.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.stranger.de: Greetings. Would you like some help surviving in these frigid wastes?
reputation.millenaire.inuits.familiarity: Your presence has not gone unnoticed. Stay peaceful and we will do the same.
We've seen you around here before. Feel free to stay a while and warm up.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.regular_vis: We're happy to see you again, $name.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.fellow_surv: Ah, it's good to see that you're still alive and surviving well!
reputation.millenaire.inuits.favourite_t: Everyone here is glad to see you. Have you brought anything exciting with you this time?
reputation.millenaire.inuits.friend_of_v: You have shown yourself a worthy companion. You can find many friends here, $name.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.blood_broth: You have done much to assist us, and we are glad to repay your efforts. You have our trust.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.one_of_us.d: The spirits have blessed us with you. They have decreed that you are part of our family now, and I feel they've made the right choice.
reputation.millenaire.inuits.natural_lea: $name, you have gained the trust and respect of the Inuit people. They will follow you anywhere.

travelbook.millenaire.byzantines.culture: The Byzantines claim they are the true Romans and are very proud of their characteristic architecture, disciplined military and the masterful icons they craft to worship the Saints. Some say they are a little too proud of their achievements.
travelbook.millenaire.byzantines.village: This skilled villager builds beautiful civilized buildings for the village, unlike the nearby desolate shacks built by those barabaric fools.
The army smith crafts mighty weapons for the village.
Some argue that the artisan wives are more skillfull than their husbands.
The baron earns his riches off the backs of his subjects, but nevertheless is invaluable in managing the daily needs of the village.
The baroness' duties are way to important to be listed here - thats what she said.
This boy will grow up to become a civilized citizen.
Former leader of a hundred men. He does not want to talk about about the reason for his demotion.
He secures the growth of carrots for the original Imperial bread. And some carrots.
She makes and markets the original Imperial bread.
The fisherman fishes for fish, kind of self-explanatory.
This girl will grow up to become a civilized citizen.
The guard sometimes regrets choosing a wife over full training to become a soldier.
The host is a master in wine making. His wine is the best on this side of the Bosporus.
The hostesse is a master in food making. Her speciality are the famous souvlakis.
She enjoyed great education in Iconography and writing - though she could make more use of that.
Lumbermen cut down trees for valuable Imperial wood.
The masons favourite material is diorite - he is even able to turn it into quartz or extravagant mosaics.
This merchant sells weaponry and armoury. The Byzantine armyforge is sure that local made Byzantine tools are superior though.
This local merchant secures the flow of goods in his village through clever trade deals with neighbouring settlements.
This merchant sells dyes of all colours and paintings, though buying and using the paintings is considered a Heresy. Be careful.
This merchant sells foods and the infamous Malvasia wine, which magically increases the birthrate of Byzantine villages.
This merchant sells stone, sandstone and Byzantine tiles - All the materials aspiring Byzantine architects dream of.
This merchant sells Icons of all sizes and invaluable frescos. Centurios pray for them to come.
This merchant sells carpets of all colours and Byzantine wool and silk clothes. Most male villagers fear for their savings.
Daily life and prayer are led by the Metropolitan in Religious villages.
This Byzantine miner mines valuable blocks for his village.
The monks support the Metropolitan in his daily business and are painting beautiful frescos.
The village pastor translates the will of God for the other villagers and makes sure children are guided to the faith, too.
Like a normal soldier, but free to hire for the leader. And for everyone else, unfortunately.
The seamster weaves carpets from wool and Icons from silk, both of superior quality.
The seamstress grows dandelions and creates clothes for the village.
Every time that a sheep eats grass, the shepherd shears it. Or he slaughters it. Better stay away from him.
The silk farmer grows silkworms and is a master in Iconography.
The smelter mastered the highly complex mechanics of using furnaces. Other villagers shudder in awe.
The soldier sometimes regrets choosing full training over marrying a beautiful woman.
He forges the quality tools that make empires.
The wives do the household, cook the Byzantine meals, harvest grapes and share the latest gossip.
The worker helps out the architect in building. Doing the same thing, he does not understand why the latter enjoys a higher status.
A village owned by a player who has earned the trust of the Byzantine people.
Led by a Centurio in a massive fortress, the military village produces fine armoury, weaponry, olive oil and wine.
Led by a Metropolitan, the religious village is known for their church, agricultural products and fine clothes from wool and silk.
Led by a Baron, the trading village is built around a market sqaure and features fine wool and silk clothes and Malvasia wine.
travelbook.millenaire.byzantines.buildin: In this well laid out grove Acacias are grown, serving as the prime fuel of the imperial furnaces.
In this small grove Acacias are grown, despite the Byzantines not liking the colour of its wood.
Just because this old place of worship seems to be plundered for building materials does not mean you should, too.
This theatre seems to have had its last play aeons ago, but the clothes in its chest suggest otherwise.
The house of the house builder who creates housing for the houseless. Of superior Byzantine quality, he added.
In the archives, all private information of the villagers are shown. If the villagers were literate, this building might spark a revolution.
This lone Byzantine watchtower is a manifestation of the Roman claim to power.
This field grows carrots. There is nothing more about it.
Not as big as a full church, but the local pastor assured that you get the same salvation when visiting a church service here.
A proud monument which is slowly growing to the sky and closer to God. It serves as the center of religious villages.
Why settle for a small shrine?
This house features a loom to weave fine clothes, carpets and Icons. As purple is insufficient, dandelions are grown for yellow dye.
The farm is composed of a large house and a silo to be able to save wheat from mouses, which are yet to be seen in this world.
Fish, squid and snails appear magically in this pond. The Byzantines find use for all of them.
The center of military villages. By personal request of the Centurio the architect tries to resemble the Theodisian walls.
The Byzantine ladies could get away with planting tulips here, if it weren't for you flower-stealing kids.
This house is a personal "Thank you" from Ticlon for helping us with Millénaire.
The inn houses local merchants that keep the village economy up and running.
The blushed occupant could not explain why the watchtower is smaller than the trees surrounding it.
The center of trading villages. This heavily integrated townsquare provides a save harbour for traders and villagers alike.
Built for guiding ships in a world that lost the knowledge of building ships.
Among the most common human outposts you find in the lands. The Byzantines just love their sheep!
Foreign merchants visit this market to sell their rare goods.
In this house and workshop, the mason performs his miracles with diorite and quartz.
The mine is filled with a near unlimited supply of stone and diorite. Enough, that the worker needs to helps out from time to time.
A watchtower to indicate that the surrounding lands belong to Rome only.
Among the most common human outposts you find in the lands. But something is odd about this one.
Olives are gathered here to be pressed into this Mediterranean speciality with various uses.
The Byzantines brought their most famous tree into this new world.
A beautiful little park showcasing the wealth of a village.
In this well layed out grove spruces are grown, which are used for the interior of Byzantine buildings.
In this small grove spruces are grown, as the Byzantines absolutely love the colour of its wood.
In this tiny grove spruces are grown, primarily for burning the wood.
The bad isolation of this watchtower makes its occupant quite uncomfortable.
This house is perfect to show that you have accumulated some wealth.
This massive plot comes with the guarantee that the local villagers won't tear down your buildings there.
Buying this small hut is a good deal if you want to join the local village for some time.
This large plot comes with the guarantee that the local villagers won't tear down your buildings there.
This small plot comes with the guarantee that the local villagers won't tear down your buildings there.
A mighty fortress owned by a player, showcasing the his dominance over the surrounding area.
The pastor enjoys a life in luxury in this mansion, which also features facilities to write books, paint icons and frescos.
The poorer wives need to gather sand, gravel and clay in this pit - because sandstone is not found outside of deserts.
The most favourite animal of the Byzantines are pampered here.
The silk farm is composed of sericultures, growing silkworms, to allow the Byzantines to create valuable Icons and clothes.
Stuffed with furnaces, the smeltery serves as a resource hub for stone, glass and bricks.
Probably the most visited building in a given village and the birthplace of delicate Malvasia wine.
In this forge civilian tools are created to serve imperial needs, speeding up various goals.
Manifested Late Roman Decadence. Don't even try to call it otherwise.
Striding through the vineyards enhance the mood. Even when it is just the thought of a sweet bottle of Malvasia wine later that day.
Serving as the home of a village guard, the watchtower ensure protection for the whole village.
This field grows large amount of wheat to secure imperial bread production at the windmills.
In this world, wheat does not need to be grinded and bread does not need to be baked. But the windmill looks cool.
This small hut is the home of the hardworking lumberman and his wife. Its location is a compromise of the couple.
Not as luxurious as an architect studio but better than the miner's place - this building is as much of a compromise as the worker himself.
The central workshop is an important hub for sand, sandstone and paths. It is run by the hardworking Byzantine wives.

travelbook.millenaire.indian.culture.des: Indian villagers prepare tasty food from rice and spices, under the protection of the mighty Rajput warriors. They seem very devotated to their many gods, though they rue the loss of their sacred river, the Holy Ganges.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.villager.me: This adivasi, or tribal, merchant visits nearby villages to sell his community's goods.
This exotic merchant from far-away Arabia specialises in luxury goods.
An old village woman, this merchant specialises in selling hot and spicy Indian delicacies.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.ad: A small farm nested in the jungle where an adivasi, or tribal, family grows crops.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.ar: The village archives, where the identity and occupation of all villagers are careful registered.
A forge dedicated to supplying weapons and armours to the local Rajput warriors.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.ba: Filled with the smell of spices and other exotic goods, this bazaar welcomes traders from all over the world.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.br: In this lowly but essential Indian building, mud bricks are left to dry in the sun to provide materials for the village's buildings.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.ch: The large and comfortable house of the village chief also serves as the village's main warehouse and trading centre, to the chief's great benefit.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.de: This small outpost in the desert hosts a lonely merchant selling goods to the occasional traveler.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.fo: A simple village forge, producing unassuming but efficient tools for the village.
This massive fort is an enduring testament to the Rajput generals' love of sandstone.<ret><ret>Players have been known to weep looking at the costs of later upgrades.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.gi: Complete with a cake, this little house rewards players that contributed to Millénaire.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.gr: Surrounded by brick walls, this grove provides the village with acacia wood.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.gu: This simple guest house hosts visiting traders in villages too small to have an inn.

travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.la: A peasant house built on a large plot, it provides space for a second family house with a shared courtyard.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.lo: This shrine was built in an isolated spot in a particularly auspicious location.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.lu: The home of a lumberman and his wife, simple but comfortable.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.pa: Possibly the most important building in the village, for it is here that the villagers grow the rice that forms the basis of all their food.
This luxurious palace is fit for the raja that inhabits it. Building it takes more resources than the rest of the village put together, but it's all worth it.
A simple but clean house, ideal for the village's pandit.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.pe: Peasant houses like this one dot Indian villages. Their thick brick walls and small windows keep the summer heat away.

travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.sa: This unique-looking tree has be chosen by the mysterious Sadhu for his retreat away from society. Its distinctive tall, leave-covered trunk can be seen from far away.
This little trading outpost was lost to the advancing desert long ago. Its chests might still hold some riches.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.sc: The house and workshop of the village sculptor, famous for his impressive carvings of Hindu gods and goddesses.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.so: A house for a village soldier, everything needed for a good nap between two patrols.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.sp: This unassuming plot of land is vital to the villagers' well-being: it's here that they grow the spices that give flavour to their food.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.su: It's here that the production of the delicious rasgullas begin, with the growth of precious sugar cane.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.ta: This impressive water tank keeps the village's crops supplied in water throughout the year.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.vi: A handsome structure of stone and sandstone to host the village's protective divinities.
This tree planted near the centre of the village provides shade in hot summer days.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.we: A deep well to better fetch the water required by the villagers.
Rice is a versatile grain used in a multitude of Indian cuisine. Vegetarian and Murgh Curry all require rice as part of their recipes.
travelbook.millenaire.indian.building.co: A small field where the Indians plant the miraculous cotton and flowers to dye it with.

travelbook.millenaire.inuits.culture.des: The Inuit are a hardy and resourceful people, capable of surviving in some of the harshest of environments. They thank the spirits for their blessings of warm fires and delicious meats that keep them going strong out in the frozen wastes.
travelbook.millenaire.inuits.villager.in: Everybody helps in Inuit villages, this young boy does what he can to aid the survival of his people. He knows if he doesn't then everyone could die.
The carver's skilled hands have been trained to carve exquisite items of bone and stone.
Inuit are able to take any part of an animal and transform it into something edible, just don't look at their food too closely.
Harvesting food from the ground is unusual for the Inuit, but not unheard of.
When not hunting animals of the land they hunt animals of the sea, the Inuit people enjoy both fishing and eating fish.
Everybody helps in Inuit villages, this young girl does what she can to aid the survival of her people. She knows if she doesn't then everyone could die.
Hunters venture out in the frozen tundra to bring back delicious meat to share with their community. Meat brings strength.
Many Inuit villagers will take on various roles like construction, goods transportation, and other small tasks in order to keep their community alive.
This local merchant wanders the wilderness hoping to find people with which to trade his wares for things his village needs to survive.
This lost carver decided to make the best of their situation and work on their skills alone.
This lost fisherman has made a home upon a lake that is plentiful in food.
Hunts can last for weeks or even more. Hunters often take shelter in snow igloos during their hunt.
The great peril of our existence lies in the fact that our diet consists entirely of souls.
This lost lumberman keeps his mind on his work and with that he has built himself an amazing home.
This shaman has left his village to commune with the spirits of this new world.
This lumberman chops trees so that his village may be equipped with enough firewood and materials to survive out in the cold.

travelbook.millenaire.inuits.building.po: Careful! Polar bears are known to live here!
travelbook.millenaire.inuits.building.sa: An igloo built out of sand by some very lost Inuit who decided to settle and start a family.
travelbook.millenaire.inuits.building.sh: House of the village shaman, adorned with trinkets and fetishes that help him commune with helpful spirits.
The center of an Inuit religious village, one that stands as an offering to the spirits in order to guarantee success in the unforgiving wilderness.
travelbook.millenaire.inuits.building.so: A hole in the ground that the Sodder and his family call home. Where else can you get enough dirt for sod than a hole in the ground?
travelbook.millenaire.inuits.building.ta: The center of the Inuit hunting village, the Inuit who lives here will tan any leather you give him into useable hide.
travelbook.millenaire.japanese.culture.d: The Heian people are from a group of islands in the vast sea. They call their home "Nihon", meaning the "origin of the sun". This culture is known for their craftsmanship, disciplined warriors and grand literature.
There is a hidden cave used by bandits to ambush travels. Warning be careful!
Watch out for an Japanese fort that has overrun by bandits. Warning stay away!
Sentou are a public bathing area for the people of the village.
Youkeijou is where farmers raise chickens for food.
Yaba is a small targeting field to practice the Yumi.
Shoko records the village's history and information.
This Tansetsu produce mostly weapons for Bushi and Keibou.
Shugi Ie are building that produce building resource like timber, plaster and paper.
Noujou Nojo grows crop for the village and later produce into food.
Gyogyo a place to raise fish for consumption.
This Tansetsu produce mostly tools for the locals.
Kodachi a place trees are grown for resources.
Shijin are resting place for travelers and Chounin.
Daidokoro is where food is prepare and cooked.
Bourou are a lookout tower for guards.
Ichiba a place to exchange good with local and traveling Chounin.
Suiden are water filled fields for the planting and growing of rice.
A Buttou, is a tower and a place of worship for the Buddhist faith.
Noufu Ie is a common house for hyakusho to live at.
Saisekijou is a pit where ground resources are collected.
Heisha are houses for Bushi warriors.
Soushi holds the local kami of the area and a place to pray to it.
Ika Sakuba is a place where squids are collected and prepared for food.
Ido is a dug hole; where water is collected.
The Soushi are a worship places for local Kami. They protect the area and bless those who worship Shinto faith.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.culture.desc: The Maya villagers speak of a lost Golden Age, but even today their architectural skills impress. They may not master iron, but their stone-working skills are without equals, and they produce a delicious cacao-based drink!
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.villager.lon: This Maya farmer works hard to sustain his family with his small, isolated farm.
Together with her husband, this Maya woman grows crops in their small jungle farm.
This Maya shaman has chosen to live in the jungle in order to better study the natural world.
This Maya woman works with her Shaman husband in the jungle.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.villager.may: The worthless son of a bandit. His family might have had a good reason for turning to banditry, but nothing has been established at this point.
A member of an opposing city state back on Earth, this bandit works to topple the current Maya majority in this land.
This woman bandit is just as violent and lawless as her male peers.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.villager.mer: This Maya merchant sells a wide array of foods, including delicious maize, wah, and masa.
This merchant shows off his stores of animal goods and weapons, in order to help his customers survive in this world.
This wandering shaman sells goods from slain monsters, crucial for offerings to the gods.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.village.agri: Based around a Sacred Ball Court, this Maya village is focused around agriculture and the production of unique Maya foods to feed the king.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.village.mili: Surrounding a mighty Pyramid, this Maya village is focused around warfare and the production of unique Maya weapons and armor for the defense against opposing villages.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.village.reli: With a great Observatory at its center, this Maya village specializes in trade and the creation of items and decorations to appease the gods.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.building.gif: Complete with a cake, this little house rewards players that contributed to Millénaire.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.building.lon: This strange abandoned Maya structure must have been used for rituals of some kinds.
This old Maya corn farm was lost to the jungle long ago.
A lonely Maya farm, where a couple of farmers grow maize.
The jungle has reclaimed this former Maya mine.
Nobody remember which Maya King ordered the construction of this massive pyramid in the jungle.
It is no longer possible to even know the purpose of this Maya building, long ago reclaimed by the jungle.
This fancy-looking shelter was built for a shaman by a grateful Maya king.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.building.may: This Sacred Ball Court is the location of the sacred Maya ballgame, a sportive event dedicated to their Gods.
This is where the village shaman comes to perform his sacrifices to the gods.
Center for all things military, this building is the workshop of the village smithy.
Necessary for the creation of unique Maya foods, such as wah or masa.
The Maya ball courts were often used for a special ball game which also doubled as a show for the gods.
This fortified dwelling hosts a dangerous bandit family.
A hideout for Maya bandits.
This well helps increase crop harvests in the village.
Cocoa was a very important part of Maya life, and this is where it is grown.
This large Maya stone calendar documents the many cycles time goes through.
This cistern greatly improves the amount of crops harvested in a village.
Cocoa and maize were the staples of Maya crops, and this is where the latter is grown.
The workshop of the crafter, this place sells stone tools and gold ornaments.
This is the village grove, where tropical trees are grown.
This house is the home of a Maya soldier, sworn to defend his village.
Small but study houses like this provide homes to Maya peasants.
This Maya inn provides room and board to merchants visiting from nearby villages.
This unusually large peasant house can host two families.
This unusually large peasant house can host two families.
A Maya library, with records of all the villagers' occupations.
A little house occupied by the village lumberman.
This fancy market hosts merchants from far away.
It's in mines such as this that the Maya produce the endless quantities of stone their architecture requires.
A Maya observatory, used to observe the night sky and predict future events.
The house of a skilled artisan, specialised in crafting obsidian.
A massive fortified estate suitable for the richest of players.
A massive field suitable for building an impressive pyramid.
A large field where to build a decent-looking pyramid.
A large and solid house for a well-off player.
An impressive pyramid from which to rule a controlled village.
A small field suitable for a small pyramid, barely a mound.
A modest Maya house suitable for a starting player.
A massive pyramid built in honour of a Maya God, around which a religious village clusters.
This broken-down pyramid still impresses even in its ruined state.
The home of the Maya sculptor, in which he carves striking statues of Maya gods.
The strange open-air dwelling of the Maya shaman.
A little village farm, where chickens are raised for their meat.
A little shrine dedicated to a local God.
A massive temple dedicated to the patron God of the village.
A fortified watchtower from which to monitor enemy city-states.
A deep well from which to get the water to grow maize.
travelbook.millenaire.mayan.trade_good.d: Lesser cultures might see this as a brown dye, but it is so much more to the Maya: the main ingredient for the sacred Cacauhaa drink.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.culture.des: The Normans seem a hardy folk, with a hearty cooking and a liking for strong alcohol. When drunk, they speak of their lost homeland on the French coast, wherever that is, and boast of their widespread conquests in mysterious places like "England" or "Sicily".
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ab: The Abbot is a man of God tasked with keeping the Normans he leads on the straight and narrow.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.al: The famous Vif-Argent is a wise man who is known to dabble in potions and alchemy in an attempt to figure out the secrets of this bizarre land.
This alchemist' apprentice trains diligently in the ways of alchemy so that he may take up his master's craft someday.
The Alchemist is a busy man, and needs the help of his trusted assistant if he's going to reveal the mysteries of life.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ar: Nicolas de Weilbourg is a master architect from Germany who has sworn his allegiance to the Norman throne for the chance to see his name immortalised in this new land through the creation of the Norman Marvel!
A veteran knight turned to a life of crime, this bandit is much harder to defeat than his unarmored brethren.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ba: This bandit is a simple man who lives a simple life of robbery, murder, rebellion, and jaywalking, all for both the thrill and a few deniers.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.bi: This Norman bishop is a unique defender of the Marvel, as he can only move diagonally, often sniping the pieces of unsuspecting opponents.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.bo: This young boy likes spending his days playing, learning, and looking forward to growing up into a productive Norman villager.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ca: Carpenters are important to Norman villages, as they're the only ones skilled enough to work wood into Timber Frames.
The wife of a livestock farmer, she's equally important to the tending of animals.
This farmer keeps watch of his livestock consisting of cattle, pigs, and chickens. A crucial part of any Norman village.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.fa: This farmer farms wheat and carrots, providing feed for the town's livestock and grain to make bread from.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.fe: A Norman baron gone rogue, who keeps to himself in his castle, surrounded by his most trusted soldiers.
Loyalty to his baron and a nice paycheck has convinced this soldier that a life of crime really is the best life.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.gi: This young girl likes spending her days playing, learning, and looking forward to growing up into a productive Norman villager.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.gl: Glassblowers create all forms of splendid stained glass using glass and dyes.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.gu: Guards are soldiers who spend their time keeping their fellow Normans safe from harm, even if that means taking the offensive now and then.
A man of trade and business entrusted with the leadership of a village. If anyone here understands the complexities of markets and finances, it's him.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.he: The Herbalist grows flowers and turns them into dyes, and works to provide the world with a little more colour.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ho: While the vicar tends to the spiritual needs of the workers, the host tends to their emotional needs through kegs of cider.
The hostess entertains workers, soldiers, merchants, and pilgrims alike in the best way she knows how, through the power of cider, of course!
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.in: The Innkeeper's wife cooks food and brews cider for the weary travellers who wander into her inn, giving them the strength for another adventure.
The Innkeeper of this lone Inn spends his time making cider and telling boring stories about his time in the army to travellers willing to listen.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.kn: Ruling with an iron fist, the Knight does all he can to keep his subjects in line and well defended.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.la: This beautiful and graceful lady spends her time talking among the peasants, weaving tapestries, and complaining about her no-good husband.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.lo: The head of an abbey located away from Norman villages, he keeps his community safe and righteous.
Alone in his wooden hut, he tirelessly cuts down timber, dreaming of a good bottle of Calva and of steaming hot tripes.
This hardy lumberman specialises in pine trees from colder forests.
This miller located his mill next to a stream, but sadly away from other villagers.
Lonely is the life of a miner whose mine is up in the mountain... But one day, he will strike gold, he just knows it!
Under the strict guidance of his abbot, this monk lives a life of silence and prayer. For now, at least.
She cooks, she builds, she provides companionship to her husband in their lonely house.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.lu: This descendant of Norman raiders uses his impressive axe to chop down trees - most of the times.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ma: A skilled stone worker whose construction skills make the Norman Marvel possible.
This priest is tasked with keeping the Marvel's workers in good spirits and close to God.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.me: This merchant trades his wares between villages, hoping to help his Norman countrymen get all they need through clever bargains.
This merchant sells Norman art and dyes, just in case you needed a little more Norman decorations around your house.
This merchant sells Norman foods, like tripes and boudin noir, the perfect foods for any growing Norman community.
This merchant sells an array of flowers and saplings to those who want a little more nature in their lives.
A merchant from a far away land. He left his home in Denmark to wander the wilds and pursue a career in dealing magical artifacts to those with enough deniers.
This merchant sells a collection of Norman weapons and armor to those who could use a bit of Norman craftsmanship to keep them safe.
This merchant sells wools of all colors, and aims to brighten the lives of his customers.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.mi: Stone mining isn't exactly a pretty or prestigious job, but one crucial to the development of any Norman village.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.mo: This monk helps maintain the Abbey with the Abbot, often by helping manage the books, trading with travellers, and keeping the faith strong among the villagers.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.or: A member of the Grand Order of Knights, this soldier of fortune has trained his entire life in the art of warfare and is NOT to be messed with, as he wields the full might of Norman power.
This man of the faith holds the prestigious title of "Chaplain of the Grand Order of Knights," and functions as the moral backbone of the Order.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.pi: This humble Norman manages a herd of pigs with his wife, raising and slaughtering them for their delicious meat.
The wife of the pig farmer, she assists in management of the farm and its livestock.
One of the many faithful who walk the halls of the new Notre Dame hoping to find a closer connection to God.
One of the many faithful who walk the halls of the new Notre Dame hoping to find a closer connection to God.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.pr: The Christian faith is a core component of the life of any Norman, and this Priest does his duty by spreading the word of God among the populace.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.se: The steward entrusted with the leadership of this agricultural community. He lives with with his wife in his luxurious manor.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.sh: A shepherd who has dedicated his life to keeping watch over a flock of sheep, providing the village with wool and mutton.
The wife of a shepherd who knows that a happy sheep is a productive sheep. She assists her husband in caring for the flock.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.sm: The Norman blacksmith creates a wide array of tools, weapons, and other metal objects that keep a village functioning properly.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.vi: The head cleric of the Notre Dame. Don't feel ashamed if you thought he was the Bishop.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.we: The weaver is a craftsman who has dedicated his life to working with wool and dyes to create beautiful carpets to decorate Norman buildings.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.wi: The backbone of any community, the humble Norman wives are tasked with keeping the villagers fed, erecting structures, transporting goods, and making sure the Norman way of life is possible in this new world.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.villager.ci: This jolly villager is reponsible for producing cider and calva from the bitter apples in his orchard. No Norman festival would be the same without him!
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.agr: A village where tasty food is produced under the vigilant eyes of the Seneschal for stockpiling in his fancy manor.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.art: Centered on a mighty Guild Hall, this village specialises in fancy buildings and proper craftsmanship.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.bou: A somewhat self-sufficient village build around a fort.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.con: A village owned by a player who has earned the trust of the Norman people.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.wal: A village owned by a player who has earned the trust of the Norman people, with walls to keep intruders out.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.ecc: Extending around an abbey, this village exists to serve the monks' material needs in exchange for salvation, in the next world if not in this one.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.gro: The centre of a thriving network of hamlets, this village holds the more advanced buildings.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.ham: A small abbatial hamlet at the periphery of a Gros Bourg.
A small hamlet focused on growing food for the nearby Gros Bourg.
A small hamlet where villagers dig stone and produce construction goods to support the nearby Gros Bourg.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.mil: A village surrounding a military fort and providing the garrison with food and weapons.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.village.not: Centered on the massive Norman Cathedral, this village supports the Marvel's construction and hosts visiting pilgrims.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ab: Once a thriving mill, this is now little more than a husk.
This little mine was abandoned long ago after its ore veins ran dry.
A lookout established by a local lord, it has long since been abandoned and forgotten.
A magnificent Norman Cathedral for the New World, designed by a famous architect on the basis of the Abbaye aux Hommes in Caen.
The center of a Norman religious village, providing a home to the Abbot and his assistant.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.al: Home of the Alchemist, where he sleeps when he's not trying to break the universe with his experiments.
The workshop of an apprentice alchemist, where he performs his experiments that border on the edge of heresy.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.an: A mysterious anomaly, definitely not Normand in origin.
A mysterious anomaly, definitely not Normand in origin.
A mysterious anomaly, definitely not Normand in origin.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ar: The village archives keep tabs on the villagers and their current tasks.
The workshop of the village blacksmith, dedicated to the creation of weapons and armor.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ba: The bakery is where the legendary Norman bread is baked.
A den of nefarious bandit activity.
A lone tower that houses highwaymen.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ca: The home of the carpenter and birthplace of the iconic Norman timber frames.
A home for the village's collection of livestock, and the farmer, of course.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ch: The home of a chicken farmer and his plentiful poultry.
A place for the village's faithful to congregate and listen to the priest's next sermon.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.fe: The Bandit Baron and his lackeys live here.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.fo: The workshop of the village blacksmith.
The center of a Norman military village, a fort perfect for keeping out French and English armies. Also works with angry peasants.
This fountain provides a pretty sight to both locals and visitors of the village.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.gi: Complete with a cake, this little house rewards players that contributed to Millénaire.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.gl: This is the home of the glassblower, where the spends his time creating stained glass.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.gr: This grove is worked by a lumberman, and is the primary source of wood for the village.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.gu: A house for soldiers. This functions as both a place rest and as a command center.
A little room occupied by the guards of the fortress.
A place for the wandering merchant to sit down and take a break from wandering.
The center of an Industrial Norman village, and hub of commerce for the Norman people.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.in: A resting point for traders both local and foreign.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.la: A large fort, with extensive habitable quarters and thick walls to keep enemy raiders at bay.
The ultimate place for leisure and relaxation when you've decided to take a break from work.
A large house for soldiers. only a few privileged soldiers can sleep between these walls.
A place for the average pilgrim, worker, or other traveller to stay as they behold the majesty of the new Notre Dame.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.lo: This isolated abbey hosts monks committed to a life of prayer away from temptations.
This small road house has a room for weary travelers.
A section of the forest where a lumberman works.
A section of the taiga where a lumberman works.
This welcoming inn provides food and shelter to travelers.
A simple hut in the woods occupied by a lumberman and his wife.
A little lumberman's hut lost in the taiga.
A water mill installed away from major settlements, but visited by surrounding farmers.
A little mine up in the mountains, next to particular ore veins.
A small orchard where the lumberman cultivates apple trees and his wife produces cider.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.lu: Home of the village lumberman and his family.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ma: The center of the Norman Agricultural village, and the perfect place for the Senechal and his wife to live.
A lively place for merchants and their potential customers to mingle.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.pa: The mysterious Panthéon, a massive building of unknown origin that lists all the contributors to Millénaire.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.pi: Home of the pig farmer, his wife, and their multitude of pigs.
A large hall capable of hosting many pilgrims.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.pl: A fancy estate designed for very wealthy players, with all the comforts of a large mansion.
An old-fashioned military fort for controlled villages, no longer used.
A huge field that can be purchased to build a palace on.
A large field that can be purchased to build a mansion on.
A large fort and impressive fort from which a player can play the village lord.
A large village house up for purchase, fit for a well-off player.
A small field that can be purchased to build a little pieds à terre.
A small village house, perfect for a starting player.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.pr: Home of the village priest, where he rests between sermons.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.qu: How so many blocks come out of this simple hole in the ground is a mystery best left to the Minecraft gods.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.re: The stately residence of the cathedral's bishop. Such luxury honours God, in ways too complicated to explain to mere peasants.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ru: Who knows what happened here? Only ruins and a little loot is left.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.sh: A farm for the raising and slaughtering of both chickens and sheep.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.ta: A place for the average Norman to relax and unwind with a stiff cider and the company of friends.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.wa: The warehouse from which the construction of the marvel is planned. The architect built himself a small adjoining room, to ensure he is always close to his workers.
A place for guards to keep an eye on the horizon for enemies and threats to the village.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.we: The house of the town weaver, where they turn wool into beautiful carpets.
The well helps Norman farmers keep their crops regularly irrigated, providing them with a boost to land fertility, and thusly, larger crop yields.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.wo: Accommodation for the skilled workers involved in the cathedral's construction. It's not luxurious, but they are very dedicated.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.sm: A small orchard where the village's lumberman gather apples and produce cider. Used by villages without access to a proper cidery.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.la: A cidery with an attached orchard, in which a cider producer gathers apple to make cider. Once upgraded with a distillery, also produces calva.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.bo: A border post to welcome visitors and warn them to behave.
A border post to welcome visitors and warn them to behave.
A border post to welcome visitors and warn them to behave.
travelbook.millenaire.norman.building.fu: A mighty wall to keep the Normans' enemies at bay.
A mighty wall to keep the Normans' enemies at bay.
A mighty wall to keep the Normans' enemies at bay.
A mighty wall to keep the Normans' enemies at bay.

travelbook.millenaire.seljuk.culture.des: The Seljuks, a Turkish dynasty with strong and disciplined soldiers ruling the near east. This culture has stunning architecture and delicious cuisine. It lives according to the rules of Islam.
travelbook.millenaire.seljuk.villager.tu: This man spends his days crafting Turkish armor and weapons in a way that only a Turk could.
This bandit is a man who lives a simple life of robbery, murder, rebellion, and jaywalking, all for both the thrill and a few deniers.
The leader of a bandit group that is well skilled in robbery and combat.
When this boy grows up he might become a soldier, a blacksmith, a farmer or even a man of God, but that will take a while.
A creator of fantastic culinary delights, you can expect to find him making Pide, Ayran, and Lokum.
Wife of the village cook, this woman helps out by acquiring the ingredients and selling the results.
A commoner with a very important job. Cotton can be used almost anywhere.
Beef is a staple of Turkish cuisine. That makes the cattle farmer an important job in Turkish society.
Cattle farming is a tough job, and the farmer wouldn't be able to do all the work without his wife!
Is it luck, skill, or perhaps a blessing from above? Whatever it is, this man is able to pull baskets full of fish from a tiny pond.
She might be small now, but she'll become a crucial part of her community after she grows up.
The emir, proud and strong, defends his village and his people with honor.
This clever farmer,with knowledge acquired over the years, keeps his village feed.
This man of God has dedicated his life to spreading the Prophet Muhammad's teachings and strengthening the faith of the villagers.
The Hoca's wife serves as a role model for the village's female community.
This man of God has dedicated his life to spreading the Prophet Muhammad's teachings and strengthening the faith of the villagers.
The Imam's wife serves as a role model for the village's female community.
Trade is the lifeblood of any village. This merchant trades with nearby villages in order to improve his home village.
Sometimes the best place for cattle is far away from his village. This man has decided to put his cows over his need for social interaction.
Sometimes the best place for farms is far away from his village. This man and his family decided to put thier farm over thier need for social interaction.
A very proud man with honor, without him the trade could not be maintained.
This is man looking for that special ore vein that can only be found in the wilderness.
An honorable companion of the trader, his job is to keep the trader safe.
Wood is useful as both a versatile building material and a source of fuel, and it's this guy's job to keep his village's stores full with wood.
An artist in his free time, this merchant sells a wide array of paintings and beautiful carpets.
This merchant has traveled from his home to share his culinary masterpieces with the world - for a price.
A stonemason in his free time, this merchant sells a wide array of bricks and stone for other hobbyists and decorators.
This merchant can be found selling his botanical wares at a market. He hopes to make a profit off of flowers and saplings he grew himself.
Formerly a blacksmith for the army, today he sells his goods in markets.
Coming from a line of shepherds, this merchant regularly has far more wool than he knows what to do with.
Millers turn wheat into freshly baked bread.
His job is to mine the stone and provide the mudbricks that the village requires to grow.
The village rests on the shoulders of the humble peasant. Who else performs the menial jobs that need doing.
The village rests on the shoulders of the humble peasant. Who else performs the menial jobs that need doing.
While wealthier than her peers, she is still a peasant deep down, and really isn't much more special.
A successful man who has devoted his life to trade and good relationships, he is not missing anything.
The richest woman in town, she looks down on others, despite them being much more useful.
This shepherd does as you would expect - herding sheep and slaughtering them helal for their delicious mutton.
The wife of a shepherd is just as important as the shepherd is, as she helps feed and care for them.
Armed with a sword and a bow, this soldier is the first line of defense for the village.
This villager can turn unassuming stone and mudbricks into beautiful masterpieces fit for sultans.
A blacksmith who specializes in the tools necessary for civilized life, such as hoes and axes.
A man of wealth and prestige, he leads his village with equal amounts grace and iron resolve.
After the shepherd shears the sheep and the farmer gathers the plants, wool and cotton comes to this man to be turned into carpets and other goods.
The weaver's wife, he wouldn't be able to do without her.
travelbook.millenaire.seljuk.village.agr: A small Seljuk  village concentrating on agriculture.
A Seljuk  village concentrating on agriculture.
travelbook.millenaire.seljuk.village.art: A small village where villagers mine stone and produce decorational goods to sell them to other villages.
travelbook.millenaire.seljuk.village.mil: A Seljuk village that focuses on security, therefore also on weapons and armor.
